transcript: I went to go see water for elephants at the Alliance Theater in Atlanta, Georgia, which is a brand new world premiere musical. And this musical was visually. If you don't know water for elephants, it's a musical that's based off of a book that was turned into a movie in 2011 with Reese Witherspoon, Robert Pattinson, Kristoff vaults. It follows our main character, Jacob, who in the musicals, played by Ryan Vasquez, as he runs away to join the circus in the middle of the Great Depression. At the circus, he, of course, finds himself tied up in a love triangle because this is a romance novel, and also tries to train an elephant. Thus, the water for elephants. And this is told as sort of a memory play by an older Jacob who is looking back on his time at the circus. So you know right away that something happened at the circus, but you don't know what. And the coolest thing that this musical did was incorporate actual circus acts into the choreography and the staging, almost in a similar way to New York, New York and dance. A lot of the transitions were a Cirque axe in between scenes. Because of the memory play structure of this play, there was a lot of going back and forth between the present and the past. And the transitions between those were really cool every single time. A lot of quick changes, a lot of quick character work, and a lot Of really creative staging because of the use of these Cirque performers, and they were so talented. There were literally moments where I was holding my breath, because I was like, are they gonna do it? You know, like when you go to a circus. Only this was also a musical, which was really cool. Of course, this is a world premiere musical, so it is a show that they are still working on, even though this is after opening of its production in Atlanta, which closed the July 9th, I do feel like the writing overall just needs a little more polishing. Of course, the book needs work, but I think in this instance, also the music and lyrics. I just wanted them to push forward the narrative a little more than what they were doing. And I can get into specifics if you want. The source material on its own has one of my least favorite tropes in romance novels. But if you like the source material, you'll like the musical. Even my issues with the writing are more than made up for the fact that I thought that the melodies in the music was pretty easy to listen to. I enjoyed sitting in that theater. Ryan Vasquez and Izzy Michaela are both fantastic. If you've never seen Ryan Vasquez in a musical, this is literally the 3rd world premiere musical that I've seen him in the span of a year. He is booked and busy, y'all, but His voice is absolutely amazing, so it makes sense I would see him in 3 more shows. And the show uses a lot of puppetry. And although the puppet design is done by Camille Labar, who is the associate puppet designer to James Ortiz on both skin of Our Teeth and into the Woods, I definitely think that this show needs a little bit more polishing before going to Broadway. I definitely think it has potential, especially with the visuals. And it's playing until July 9th if you are near Atlanta to go see it.
